But is full faithfulness of the generic fiber functor for the **punctured** curve really true? Let's double-check with a more subtle example. Let X = E \ {O}, finite étale covers Y → X. Since X is affine and not proper, a finite étale cover Y may not be the restriction of an isogeny of E; it could be a cover that is ramified only at O. For example, the cover of E \ {O} given by `E' \ {O} → E \ {O}` from an isogeny at O? If Y is a finite étale cover of E \ {O}, its generic fiber is a finite étale K-algebra L/K. The normalization of E in L is a smooth projective curve C → E, which is finite flat; it may be ramified at O and elsewhere. But Y = C \ {points above O} is finite étale over E \ {O}. So covers of the punctured curve correspond to finite separable extensions L/K **unramified away from O** (ramification at O allowed). The generic fiber functor from these covers to **all** finite étale K-algebras is not essentially surjective, but it is fully faithful. Is it full? Given a K-algebra map L' → L (for covers Y, Y'), does it come from a map of covers? The map of generic fibers is a K-algebra map; it extends to a rational map C' → C over E, and since C' is proper and C is proper, it extends to a morphism (by the valuative criterion of properness). It maps the points above O to points above O? It maps the generic fiber, so yes, it maps the generic point to the generic point; the image of C' is a closed subscheme of C containing the generic point, hence all of C; and it commutes with the maps to E. It should map Y' to Y because the preimage of E \ {O} under the map is contained in Y'? If a point of Y' maps to O, that would be a point above O; but Y' is the complement of points above O, so the map of covers is defined on Y'. So fullness holds. Good.

What if Y is a finite étale cover of E \ {O} that is not the restriction of a proper cover? Any finite étale cover of a curve extends to a normal proper curve (by normalization), so it is the restriction of a finite morphism of smooth projective curves. Yes. Fullness holds.

What about **disconnected** covers? A finite étale cover Y → X can be disconnected; its generic fiber is a product of fields. A K-algebra map between products is a matrix of maps; each component extends; the map of covers extends. Fullness holds componentwise. Good.

The essential image: Covers of E \ {O} correspond to finite separable L/K unramified at all points **except possibly O**. The integral closure B of R in L is the coordinate ring of the affine curve C \ {points above O}; B is finite étale over R iff C → E is unramified at all points of E \ {O}, i.e., L/K is unramified outside O. This matches `S1750Unramified`: B = integral closure of R in L. For L/K unramified outside O, B is finite étale over R. Yes.
